summary: Henry Steel Olcott worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia University around 1848 to 1851 and founded the Theosophical Society in 1875.
Henry Sullivan Jarrett worked in history and archaeology. He served as Secretary and Member on the Board of Examiners at Fort William from around 1870 to 1892, succeeding Heinrich Blochmann.

Henry Thomas Colebrooke worked in Indology, studying under Citrapati. He served in the East India Company, Bengal Civil Service, Sadar Diwani Adalat, and Council of India, taught at Fort William College, and presided over the Royal Asiatic Society.

Herbert Cushing Tolman worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Yale, Peabody College, University of Nashville, Hobart College, and University of Louisville, and held posts at Yale, Wisconsin-Madison, North Carolina, and Vanderbilt.

Herbert Franke was a sinologist and historian. He studied under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer and attended Bonn, Humboldt University, the Seminar for Oriental Languages, and Cologne. He held posts at Cologne, Cambridge, Washington, Munich, and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.
Herbert Hope Risley worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He was educated at Winchester College around 1864 to 1869 and at New College, Oxford, from around 1869 to 1873.

Herbert Härtel specialized in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Halle and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, Museum of Asian Art, Humboldt University, and Free University of Berlin.

Herbert Niel Randle worked in Indology and philosophy. He was a professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1908–1927) and served as Librarian at the India Office and the India Office Library (1927–1949).

Herbert V. Günther worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned doctorates at Munich and Vienna, held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and served as department head at the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

Herbert Weir Smyth worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe. His teaching posts included Williams College, Johns Hopkins, Bryn Mawr College, and Harvard University.

Herman Kellgren worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux, and held a post at the University of Helsinki from around 1849 to 1856.
Herman Wirth worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Utrecht University from around 1903 to 1906, held a post at the University of Bern from around 1909 to 1916, and founded Ahnenerbe.

Hermann Beckh specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he later served as a Privatdozent from around 1911 to 1921.

Hermann Berger was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctoral and habilitation studies under Helmut Hoffmann around 1950 to 1955 and took up a post at Heidelberg University in 1965.
Hermann Beythan worked in the fields of linguistics and Indology. His education included studying under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

Hermann Bonitz was a scholar of philosophy and linguistics who studied at Leipzig University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (~1867–1888).

Hermann Brockhaus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm Schlegel. He held professorships at the University of Jena and Leipzig University, where he also served as Rektor.

Hermann Brunnhofer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Humboldt University, and Zurich under Albrecht Weber. He taught at Kuldīga Gymnasium, served as librarian at Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek, and lectured at the University of Bern.

Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from around 1858 to 1863. He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Königliches Gymnasium Zwickau from around 1868 to 1904.

Hermann Collitz worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Göttingen under August Fick, Theodor Benfey, Hermann Sauppe, and Adalbert Bezzenberger, as well as Berlin and Halle. He held academic posts at Bryn Mawr College and Johns Hopkins University.
